meta.name: Generate agile project plan PDFs from proposals with Claude and SharePoint

parameters.content:
## N8N-Project Proposal

### How it works

This workflow receives a posted project plan PDF, extracts its text, and sends the content through an AI agent to generate structured project plan insights. It parses the AI output, builds an HTML report, converts that report into a PDF using an external service, uploads the PDF to SharePoint, and sends an Outlook email notification.

### Setup steps

- Configure the webhook endpoint and ensure the posting system sends the project plan PDF in the expected binary field.
- Add Anthropic/Claude credentials for the LangChain chat model used by the AI agent.
- Update the HTML-to-PDF HTTP Request node with the real service URL, authentication, and expected request/response format.
- Connect Microsoft SharePoint credentials and configure the target site, drive, folder, and filename settings.
- Connect Microsoft Outlook credentials and configure notification recipients, sender options, and email content fields.

### Customization

Customize the AI prompt and parsing code to match your proposal format, adjust the HTML template and styling for branded reports, and change the SharePoint destination or Outlook recipients for different teams or projects.

## Receive and prepare PDF

Accepts an uploaded project plan through the webhook, extracts text from the PDF, and packages the extracted content into the structure needed for AI processing. These nodes form the leftmost input/preprocessing cluster.

## Generate and parse plan

Uses the Claude-backed LangChain agent to generate project plan insights from the extracted PDF data, then parses the AI response into usable structured plan data. The Claude model subnode is grouped with its parent AI chain because it directly powers the generation step and is spatially nested nearby.

## Build PDF report

Transforms the parsed project plan into an HTML report, prepares the HTML payload, and sends it to an external HTML-to-PDF service. This middle-right cluster handles report rendering and PDF generation.

## Store and notify

Uploads the generated PDF to SharePoint, creates the notification email content, and sends the final Outlook notification. These nodes are positioned together at the far right as the workflow’s delivery and notification cluster.

messageValues.message:
=You are an expert Agile project manager and Lean Six Sigma Black Belt specializing in legal technology. You receive a project outline and consultation notes, then produce a complete project plan as valid JSON.

OUTPUT ONLY VALID JSON. No markdown fences, no explanation, no extra text — raw JSON only.

Return a single JSON object with these top-level keys:

- client: name, company, email, phone, projectTitle, projectType, requestDescription
- projectVision: problemStatement, businessGoals (array), successMetrics (array), scope (inScope/outOfScope arrays), assumptions (array), constraints (array)
- leanSixSigma: define (problemStatement, projectCharter, ctq array, sipoc object, voiceOfCustomer array), measure (currentStateDescription, baselineMetrics array), analyze (rootCauses array, fishboneCategories object with 6 keys, prioritizedGaps array), improve (solutions array with solution/impact/effort/description, implementationApproach), control (controlPlan, kpis array, sustainmentActivities array)
- backlog: array of user stories — each has id, epic, story, acceptanceCriteria array, priority (Critical/High/Medium/Low), storyPoints, category, sprintTarget
- roadmap: array of phases — each has phase, milestone, weeksStart, weeksEnd, deliverables array, colorHex
- releases: array — each has version, name, description, sprints array, keyFeatures array, targetWeek
- sprints: array — each has number, name, goal, duration, weeksStart, weeksEnd, tasks array (task/type/hours/owner), storyPoints, definitionOfDone array
- ceremonies: standup (duration/format array/participants array/notes), sprintReview (duration/agenda array/demoChecklist array), retrospective (duration/format/categories with wentWell/needsImprovement/actionItems arrays)
- budget: development/projectManagement/techSupport/training/travel objects (each with hours, rate, total, description), subtotal, contingency (percentage:10, amount), grandTotal, paymentTerms, notes
- timeline: totalWeeks, totalSprints, estimatedStartDate, phases array
- risks: array — each has id, risk, impact, probability, score, mitigation, owner, status

Be concise. Generate only what is realistic for the actual project scope — do not pad arrays. 3-5 backlog items, 2-4 sprints, and 3-5 risks is sufficient unless the scope clearly requires more.

Budget calculation rules:
- Development: $300/hr — all custom build, automation, integration work
- Project Management: $150/hr — typically 15-20% of total project hours
- Tech Support: $250/hr — setup, configuration, troubleshooting
- Training: $500/hr — includes all course materials
- Travel: reimbursed at actual cost + $50/hr for travel time. Estimate only if relevant.
- Contingency: always add 10% of subtotal
- Generate realistic hour estimates based on the actual scope described

Generate specific, realistic content based on the actual project outline — not generic placeholders. Extract client name, company, email, and phone directly from the document text.
